title.narrative: Support to conflict-affected IDPs recently returned or relocated in Sheraro, North West Tigray.

description.narrative: ltpgtDue to the severe conflict that took place in the Tigray region, the schools in Sheraro were occupied by internally displaced persons (IDPs). The proposed multi-sector project with CCCM, education, protection, WASH, and shelter interventions, including back-to-school campaigns and awareness-raising activities to increase enrollment, especially among out-of-school children and their caregivers. In addition, IRC will address the essential repair, fixtures, and cleanup/painting needs identified through assessments not covered by Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), maintenance of water supply and sanitation facilities, decommissioning emergency WASH facilities, establishment/strengthening of School WASH committee. This includes repairing broken windows, doors, and furniture and cleaning up broken glass, garbage, and hazardous materials in classrooms and school compounds. Furthermore, IRC will provide necessary school furniture such as blackboards, desks, chalk, and dusters based on the respective needs assessment of the four targeted schools. ltbrgtThe project also ensures the protection and safe access to critical, integrated, inclusive essential services to the displaced population and host community members while effecting the following activities. Identification and support to children in need of CP /PSS, including Unaccompanied and Separated Children (UASC) and out-of-school children through case management and referral linkages, vulnerability screening, including referral to relevant services, emergency fund/cash support to address emergency cash needs to meet the needs and lifesaving supplies of newly born babies whose mothers passed away due to complicated pregnancy and/or during delivery, for purchasing medicine, and transportation cost for children with referrals into a higher hospital (into Mekelle and Axum referral Hospitals) and material support. The UASC and other vulnerable children without appropriate care will receive structured psychosocial support services and recreational activities through the established safe healing and learning spaces (SHLSs) in Adi-Abay site. In addition, the IRC will provide curriculum-based social and emotional learning (SEL) for internally displaced children in a state of psychological distress and traumatized situation. The IRC will also provide parenting skill training for parents/caregivers. The project will also focus on capacity building and awareness raising on CP, GBV, PSEA, and prevention of family separation to strengthen the existing child protection committee and ensure the sustained community-based protection by establishing and strengthening child right clubs and further delivery of mobile case management service across the four target schools through trained case workers. ltbrgtThe project will also continue to target people solely based on identified acute, lifesaving needs for shelter, cash for rent, or a combination of both. For this purpose, the priority groups are IDPs who will be relocated from schools to settlement sites and supported with Shelter and Cash for rent response should be aligned with the Settlement type of the displaced population to prevent secondary displacements and to ensure that they can live with security, safety, and dignity.ltbrgtIRC has been working and will continue to work closely with target woreda Education Offices, Women and Children’s Affairs Offices as well community representatives like members of Parent Teacher Associations (PTA), CP committees and child rights club members to identify/verify prioritized needs conducted thorough assessment, across the target schools and set participatory and transparent selection criteria for target clients. This proposed project will be implemented in partnership with Organization for Social Services, Health and Development (OSSHD). OSSHD is one of the leading local partner implementing CCCM activities in North West Tigray and it is the cluster coordination lead for the region.lt/pgt
